source_text: Μὴ δή, ὦ ἀδελφοί, κακόν τι εἴπητε εἰς ἐκεῖνον τὸν ἐσταυρωμένον, μηδὲ χλευάσητε αὐτοῦ τοὺς μώλωπας, οἷς ἰαθῆναι πᾶσι δυνατόν, ὡς καὶ ἡμεῖς ἰάθημεν . Καλὸν γάρ, ἢν πεισθέντες τοῖς λόγοις περιτμηθῆτε τὴν σκληροκαρδίαν, ἥν οὐχὶ δι᾿ ὑμῶν ἐγγινομένην γνώμην ἔχετε, ἐπειδὴ εἰς σημεῖον ἦν δεδομένη, ἀλλ᾿ οὐκ εἰς δικαιοπραξίας ἔργον, ὡς οἱ λόγοι ἀναγκάζουσι. Συμφάμενοι οὖν μὴ λοιδορῆτε ἐπὶ τὸν υἱὸν τοῦ θεοῦ, μηδὲ Φαρισαίοις πειθόμενοι διδασκάλοις τὸν βασιλέα τοῦ Ἰσραὴλ ἐπισκώψητέ ποτε, ὁποῖα διδάσκουσιν οἱ ἀρχισυνάγωγοι ὑμῶν, μετὰ τὴν προσευχήν. Εἰ γὰρ ὁ ἁπτόμενος τῶν μὴ εὐαρέστων τῷ θεῷ ὡς ὁ ἁπτόμενος κόρης τοῦ θεοῦ , πολὺ μᾶλλον ὁ τοῦ ἠγαπημένου καθαπτόμενος . Ὅτι δὲ οὗτος αὐτός ἐστι, καὶ ἱκανῶς ἀποδέδεικται. Καὶ σιγώντων αὐτῶν εἶπον· Ἐγώ, ὦ φίλοι. καὶ τὰς γραφὰς λέγω νῦν ὡς ἐξηγήσαντο οἱ ἑβδομήκοντα· εἰπὼν γὰρ αὐτὰς πρότερον ὡς ὑμεῖς αὐτὰς ἔχετε, πεῖραν ὑμῶν ἐποιούμην πῶς διάκεισθε ἤδη τὴν γνώμην. Λέγων γὰρ τὴν γραφήν, ἣ λέγει· Οὐαὶ αὐτοῖς, ὅτι βεβούλευνται βουλὴν πονηρὰν καθ᾿ ἑαυτῶν εἰπόντες· ὡς ἐξηγήσαντο οἱ ἑβδομήκοντα ἐπήνεγκα· Ἄρωμεν τὸν δίκαιον, ὅτι δύσχρηστος ἡμῖν ἐστιν· ἐμοῦ ἐν ἀρχῇ τῆς ὁμιλίας καὶ εἰπόντος ὅπερ ὑμεῖς εἰρῆσθαι βούλεσθε, εἰπόντες· Δήσωμεν τὸν δίκαιον, ὅτι δύσχρηστος ἡμῖν ἐστιν . Ἄλλα δέ τινα ἐπράξατε, καὶ οὐ δοκεῖτέ μοι ἐνηκόως τῶν λόγων ἐπακηκοέναι. Ἀλλ᾿ ἐπεὶ καὶ νῦν ἤδη ἡ ἡμέρα πέρας ποιεῖσθαι μέλλει, πρὸς δυσμὰς γὰρ ἤδη ὁ ἥλιός ἐστι, καὶ ἔν τι προσθεὶς τοῖς εἰρημένοις παύσομαι· τοῦτο δ᾿ αὐτὸ καὶ ἐν τοῖς εἰρημένοις μοι ἐρρέθη, ἀλλὰ πάλιν αὐτὸ ἐπεξεργάσασθαι ἄν δίκαιον εἶναί μοι δοκεῖ.
pass_a_gloss: Do not, my brothers, speak anything evil against the one who was crucified, nor mock his bruises, by which it is possible for all to be healed, as we also have been healed. For it is good, if having been persuaded by the words, you will circumcise the hardness of heart, which is not coming to be through your opinion, since it was given as a sign, but not as a work of righteousness, as the words compel. Therefore, having agreed, do not rail against the Son of God, nor, obeying the Pharisee teachers, ever despise the King of Israel, as your synagogue rulers teach after the prayer. For if the one touching the things not pleasing to God is as the one touching the pupil of God's eye, much more so the one touching the beloved. That this one is he, has been sufficiently demonstrated. And as they were silent, I said: I, my friends, now speak the scriptures as the seventy interpreted them; for having spoken them previously as you have them, I was making a test of you, to see how you are already disposed in your opinion. For saying the scripture which says: Woe to them, because they devise an evil plan among themselves, saying: Let us take away the righteous, for he is troublesome to us, as the seventy interpreted it, I praised, saying: Let us take away the righteous, for he is troublesome to us; at the beginning of my conversation and having said what you wish to have been said, having said: Let us bind the righteous, for he is troublesome to us. But you have done something else, and it does not seem to me that you have heard the words attentively. But since now the day is about to come to an end, for the sun is already in the west, and adding something to what has been said, I will stop; and this very thing was said to me also in what was said, but again it seems to me that it would be right to work it out.

pass_b_english: My brothers, do not speak anything evil against the one who was crucified, and do not mock his bruises, by which it is possible for all to be healed, just as we also have been healed. For it is good, if, having been persuaded by the words, you will circumcise the hardness of your heart—a hardness that does not arise from your own opinion, since it was given as a sign, not as a work of righteousness, as the words compel. Therefore, having agreed, do not rail against the Son of God, nor, obeying the Pharisee teachers, ever despise the King of Israel, as your synagogue rulers teach after the prayer. For if the one who touches the things not pleasing to God is like the one who touches the pupil of God's eye, how much more so the one who touches the Beloved. That this one is he has been sufficiently demonstrated.

And while they were silent, I said: "I, my friends, now speak the scriptures as the Seventy interpreted them. For having spoken them previously just as you have them, I was testing you to see how you are already disposed in your opinion." For saying the scripture which says: "Woe to them, because they devise an evil plan against themselves, saying: 'Let us take away the righteous, for he is troublesome to us,'" as the Seventy interpreted it, I added: "Let us take away the righteous, for he is troublesome to us." At the beginning of my discourse, and having said what you yourselves wanted to be said, you said: "Let us bind the righteous, for he is troublesome to us." But you have done something else, and it does not seem to me that you have listened attentively to the words. But since the day is now about to come to an end—for the sun is already in the west—and adding something to what has been said, I will stop; and this very thing was said to me also in what was said, but again it seems right to me to work it out.
